title: Exact finite-free scalar extension on the two finite-coefficient sites
statement:
Let $W$ be a Noetherian scheme, let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of finite commutative rings such that $B$ is free of finite rank $r$ over $A$, and choose either the small etale site or the small pro-etale site of $W$. Use constant ring sheaves, module sheaves, and their ordinary unbounded derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $T=-\otimes_A^LB$ for derived change of rings [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] and $U$ for restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Both ordinary scalar extension and $U$ are exact. Their termwise functors on complexes descend to the derived categories, the former identifies canonically with $T$, and the usual scalar unit and counit give $T\dashv U$. The functor $U$ reflects zero objects and isomorphisms. A basis $b_1,\ldots,b_r$ of $B/A$ gives the natural identification $UTK\cong K^{\oplus r}$, with inclusions induced by $k\mapsto k\otimes b_j$.

For every $K\in D(W,A)$ and $N\in D(W,B)$ there is a natural derived isomorphism
$$U(TK\otimes_B^L N)\cong K\otimes_A^L UN.$$
On K-flat representatives its forward and inverse balancing maps are $(p\otimes b)\otimes n\mapsto p\otimes bn$ and $p\otimes n\mapsto(p\otimes1)\otimes n$, respectively [def-pc-kflat-complex]. Extension of a K-flat $A$-complex is K-flat over $B$. In particular $T$ preserves bounded constructibility on the etale site [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes] and on the finite-coefficient pro-etale realization [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. If $K$ has Tor amplitude in $[a,b]$, meaning that $K\otimes_A^LF$ has cohomology only in that interval for every degree-zero module sheaf $F$, then $TK$ has Tor amplitude in the same interval [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude].

proof.text: Apply lem-sf-finite-free-scalar-tensor-calculus on the small etale and small pro-etale sites. Apply lem-sf-finite-free-scalar-derived-tensor-models to both resulting ordinary scalar packages. The same generic site lemma handles rank zero and the empty site.

For etale bounded constructibility, apply constructibleCoefficientSheaf to every cohomology sheaf. The exact-functor homology isomorphism transfers constructibility to the cohomology of D(E)K. Exact functors preserve zero objects, hence the very same cohomological bounds. For the pro-etale essential-image predicate, choose its etale origin L and isomorphism nu_A L ≅ K. The existing ordinary scalar/comparison square induces a derived natural isomorphism D(E_et) nu_B ≅ nu_A D(E_pro). Combine this with D(E_pro) of the given origin isomorphism. The extended etale origin is bounded constructible by the preceding argument.

For every degree-zero B-module sheaf F, the derived balancing isomorphism followed by the exact restriction/single-functor comparison identifies U(D(E)K tensor_B F[0]) with K tensor_A (UF)[0]. The assumed Tor interval gives concentration of the right side. Faithful exact ordinary restriction reflects concentration of cohomology by its homology comparison, so D(E)K has that same Tor interval. Fill the two FiniteFreeScalarCalculus records with these constructions; the conjunction is the requested theorem.

lean.note: The conclusion package uses the published fixed-ModuleCat sheaf presentation on both sites. Ordinary extension is composeAndSheafify of ModuleCat.extendScalars, and derived restriction is the existing exact descent. The universal field identifies exact extension descent with derived change of rings via its canonical counit. Unit, counit, basis inclusions, both local balancing formulas and the K-flat total-complex comparison are explicitly normalized. FiniteScalarDerivedTensorModels packages the derived comparison, joint naturality and cochain normalization generically, then the concrete package supplies the fixed scalar functors and its normalized sheaf balancing map. This partition of conclusions avoids expanding concrete site dictionaries and adds no hypotheses. Pro-etale bounded constructibility is the essential image of the recorded finite-value etale predicate under the published comparison. All universes of that derived comparison are explicit. No mathematical statement changes. Y5: all original conclusion data are reexported verbatim from Sheaf.Paper.FiniteFreeScalarCalculusData; theorem signature unchanged.
